finding:
PF-13's POPULATION IS 16 TEST FILES over 2 directories (test/career/mapping-field/, test/career/mapping-spec/), read out of architecture.test.ts's own phase-D predicate rather than restated here.
AND IT CORRECTS MY OWN REPORT: I quoted "170/170 on test/career/mapping-field" as PF-13's population. That is ONE of the two directories PHASE_DIRS names; 2 test files under test/career/mapping-spec/ were never in the number.
THE EXCEPTION LIST IS NOW NAMED BY TITLE (GELB §95, ruled), and the conversion is PROVEN rather than asserted: each title resolves back to the same it() line its original NUMBER resolved to, each title is unique in the file, and the instrument throws on either failure. The line numbers are kept as a legacy citation so the pin's own wording stays traceable.
THE LEGACY CITATION RESOLVES, AND IT IS FRAGILE. The pin's three line numbers each fall inside one it() — :156 -> it() at :156 (+0), :174 -> it() at :173 (+1), :140 -> it() at :136 (+4) — naming 3 distinct tests. 2 of the 3 titles say "restated" in the title itself, matching the pin's cited §12/A-F15. But 2 citation(s) sit 2 lines or fewer inside their own it(), and §93 shifted this file by +3 — all three still resolve, which I checked rather than assumed, and which is luck rather than design.
NO VERDICT (A-G36 point 2): this names a population and resolves a citation. Whether the population passes is a RUN, reported separately, and whether PF-13 is satisfied is PINK's.
